high_risk_moment: An ambiguous pedestrian or bicyclist enters the planned path during a supervised test
stakeholder: Pedestrians and cyclists on the approved test route
harm_description: A missed or delayed escalation can leave an unsafe trajectory in progress and seriously injure or kill a road user who did not choose the service.
existing_controls: The research boundary assumes a designated safety driver and named ODD, but no approved safety case or demonstrated alert-to-takeover control exists.
proposed_controls: GAP-01 must establish an approved ODD safety case, a current evidence bundle, a manual-takeover or pause instruction for each out-of-policy critical state, and an auditable driver-response record. Severity remains 5; likelihood cannot be reduced until independent evidence demonstrates the control.
human_oversight: The safety driver takes manual control immediately without waiting for the console. The remote operator sees object, trajectory, confidence, ODD, sensor-health, and freshness evidence and may pause; only the Fleet Safety Lead can authorize return after incident review.
monitoring_metric: Confirmed critical missed-escalation count per independently adjudicated critical-scenario denominator
trigger_threshold: Any confirmed critical missed escalation; zero is accepted per supervised research test week
response_action: Pause the affected route or software version, preserve the evidence record, investigate, and prevent return-to-test authorization until the safety case is re-approved.

high_risk_moment: The operator console receives road-user, ODD, or sensor evidence needed to recommend a pause
stakeholder: Pedestrians, cyclists, and other road users
harm_description: Stale, mismatched, or missing evidence can make a critical condition look safe or delay a pause recommendation, exposing road users to a preventable unsafe continuation.
existing_controls: No end-to-end evidence-freshness, source-integrity, or console safety-latch result has been demonstrated in the research stage.
proposed_controls: GAP-01 must make freshness and integrity visible to the operator, treat a failed critical check as an unsafe state, suppress a return-to-test authorization, and retain the evidence needed for review. Severity remains 5 and planned controls do not yet justify a likelihood reduction.
human_oversight: The safety driver remains responsible for immediate manual control. The remote operator can pause only after seeing the evidence state; the Fleet Safety Lead cannot reauthorize testing if the record shows failed or stale critical evidence.
monitoring_metric: Alert-evidence-integrity failure count and sampled console safety-latch audit pass rate
trigger_threshold: Any critical alert-evidence-integrity failure or any sampled safety-latch failure
response_action: Pause the affected route or software version, preserve logs, correct the evidence path, and repeat independent scenarios before re-enablement.

high_risk_moment: A safety driver receives a mode-change or critical take-over instruction while managing intended workload
harm_description: Mode confusion, overload, or a nominal acknowledgement can leave the safety driver unready to intervene promptly, putting the driver and nearby road users at risk.
existing_controls: No independent evidence shows that intended safety drivers or remote operators understand alert limits, authority, or workload effects in SafeRoute's workflow.
proposed_controls: GAP-02 must require evidence-rich alerts, explicit authority, and independent blinded scenario tests measuring response-time distributions, missed and false-alert rates, evidence comprehension, and mode comprehension. Acknowledgement alone is not accepted as readiness.
human_oversight: A safety driver can disengage automation at any time and must not wait for remote approval. The remote operator sees the availability signal and may pause; an independent assessor observes the scenario evidence and can block pilot release when a critical outcome is missed.
monitoring_metric: Critical-scenario readiness exceptions, safety-driver unavailability events, and false-alert burden
trigger_threshold: Any missed critical scenario, any unavailable safety driver, or any result outside the approved scenario-specific safety budget
response_action: Suspend the affected route or software version, notify the Fleet Safety Lead, remediate workflow or training, and repeat the independent scenario set before re-enablement.

high_risk_moment: The fleet proposes to continue or expand testing after a serious incident, near miss, or control breach
harm_description: Incomplete incident records, hidden safety-information gaps, or premature restart can expose the public to a repeat unsafe operation and undermine accountable oversight.
existing_controls: A draft incident procedure exists, but no independent restart-veto drill, complete record sample, or legal classification/incident decision has been demonstrated.
proposed_controls: GAP-05 must provide an immutable incident and decision record, an independent restart review, a no-retaliation escalation path, and a demonstrated Chief Safety Officer and assessor veto. GAP-03 must determine applicable Vietnam incident duties before pilot. Severity remains 5 and no reduction is claimed until these controls are evidenced.
human_oversight: The remote operator can halt the fleet; the Chief Safety Officer can keep testing paused; the independent assessor receives the complete event record and may veto restart. Legal counsel determines any external notification path from the final facts rather than assuming one.
monitoring_metric: Incident-record completeness, restart-approval audit pass rate, and independent-veto drill result
trigger_threshold: Any serious incident, incomplete record, failed veto drill, or independent-review objection
response_action: Pause all comparable tests, preserve evidence, obtain legal advice on any notification duty, and convene an independent restart review before any scope expansion.
